9:1013.name: Button
9:1013.description:
Purpose: Triggers an immediate action or command.

Usage: Use for primary actions like “Submit,” “Save,” or “Continue.” Limit one primary button per view.


Example: Use a primary button for “Sign Up” and a secondary button for “Learn More.”

9:1904.name: Progress Indicator
9:1904.description:
Purpose: Shows the progress of a task or process over time.

Usage: Use for uploads, downloads, or multi-step processes to provide real-time feedback.


Example: Show a progress bar while a file is uploading.

9:2230.name: Title
9:2230.description:
Purpose: Defines text hierarchy and ensures readability and brand consistency.

Usage: Apply heading, body, and caption styles according to content importance and layout needs.


Example: Use H1 for page titles and body text for content paragraphs.

9:13424.name: Data Group
9:13424.description:
Purpose: Displays data in a structured row format for lists, tables, or summaries.

Usage: Use in dashboards, reports, or any layout where aligned tabular data is presented.


Example: Show transaction records in rows within a finance dashboard.

9:2325.name: Country Flags
9:2325.description:
Purpose: Provides visual representation of countries using flag icons and emojis.

Usage: Use alongside country names, language selectors, or international data displays.


Example: Add country flags to a currency selection dropdown.

9:12391.name: Badge
9:12391.description:
Purpose: Highlights a count, status, or small piece of metadata attached to another UI element.

Usage: Use to show notifications, unread messages, or item counts. Avoid using badges for long text.


Example: Add a small badge showing “New” on a product card.

9:13419.name: slot
9:13419.description:
Purpose: Defines a flexible content area that can host variable components.

Usage: Use in layout or component templates that require reusable content placeholders.


Example: Use a slot to dynamically load different card content in a dashboard.

9:13596.name: Checkbox
9:13596.description:
Purpose: Allows users to make one or multiple selections from a list of options.

Usage: Use when users can select multiple items independently or enable/disable specific settings. Each checkbox should have a clear label describing the choice. Avoid using checkboxes when only one option is allowed — use radio buttons instead.

Example: Use checkboxes for selecting multiple interests (e.g., “Music,” “Travel,” “Sports”) in a preferences form.

9:13673.name: Cards
9:13673.description:
Purpose: Encapsulates related information into a distinct container.

Usage: Use to group visual and textual elements such as images, titles, and calls to action.
